questions.question: Describe the first Moon landing and what the Apollo astronauts did on the Moon.
questions.expected_answer: On 20 July 1969, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on it, while Michael Collins stayed in orbit. Between 1969 and 1972, twelve astronauts walked on the Moon. They collected more than three hundred and eighty kilograms of rocks and dust, set up experiments, took photographs and left footprints.

questions.question: Explain how the design of the Lunar Roving Vehicle solved two problems of driving on the Moon.
questions.expected_answer: There is no air on the Moon, so a petrol engine could not burn its fuel; the rover used batteries and an electric motor in each wheel instead. The Moon has rough, dusty ground and extreme heat and cold, so air-filled rubber tyres could burst; the rover had wheels of woven steel wire mesh that could not go flat. It also folded up to fit on the small lander, and had its own navigation system because a compass does not work on the Moon.

questions.question: What are robot rovers, and what are their advantages and disadvantages compared with astronauts?
questions.expected_answer: Robot rovers are vehicles with cameras and instruments that are controlled by people on Earth using radio signals. Robots have explored the Moon since 1970, including the far side in 2019 and near the south pole in 2023. They are cheaper and safer, because they do not need air, food, water or a way home. But people can think quickly, notice surprises and decide what to do on the spot.
